reel.name: reel-25-year-burnout
reel.caption_ig:
As a coach at $20K/mo your bottleneck isn't going to be capacity anymore. It becomes how many other people's problems you can absorb.

A coach with 25 years of experience told me he's burned out. Not by the work but by the people.

The work wasn't the problem for him. It was the late-night DMs about cheat meals. The voice notes about their boyfriend or girlfriend. The check-ins where clients cry about their body, their job, their kids.

Carrying around 200 lives for 25 years sounds good but it's hard, stressfull and burns most people out.

The coaches I studied who lasted more than 10 years all did the following 2 things →

1. They wrote a list of what they don't carry. Cheat meal guilt. Their fight with their boyfriend. Their bad day at work. They tell every new client up front: "I do fitneess and nutrition coaching. The rest stays out of our DMs."

2. Or they built an exit. Hired a second coach, a Virtual Assistant, built a team that handles everyting they don't like in the business while they keep doing what they love which most of the time is coaching.

This is what the $20K/mo online fitness coaches need to scale past this point.

reel.name: reel-hollings-unsustainable
reel.caption_ig:
Most online fitness coaches who scale had 18 months of unsustainable work nobody warned them about. And most quit at year 3.

I've studied more than 100 online fitness coaches at this point. The ones who scaled all did some version of this.

A coach told me she worked her 9-5. Came home. Went live on Instagram 3 to 4 hours every night. Posted 5 reels a week. For 18 months straight.

If you're a year in and you're not doing some version of that, you're probrably not getting the clients you want.

Here's the trap. Most online fitness coaches who run that shape for 3 years quit. The ones who survive put a deadline on it.

12 months. That's the rule. After that the unsustainable thing has to become a system →

→ Hire a content editor to chop your lives into 5 reels a week.
→ Bring in a Virtual Assistant to handle every DM that hits your inbox.
→ Switch from 4 lives a night to 2 batched posts a week.

Or you fire the unsustainable thing entirely.

Build momentum. But put a deadline on the part that eats you. Otherwise the momentum eats you.

4. Referral Rate: new clients from referrals / total new clients per quarter. If it's below 30%, your results aren't strong enough to talk about.

Block 30 minutes this Sunday. Pull these 4 numbers. They don't just measure the business. They diagnose where the leak is.

reel.name: reel-25-hour-rule
reel.caption_ig:
Most online fitness coaches working 50 hours a week charge their clients half of what they should. And the math proves it.

I've studied 100+ online fitness coaches at this stage. The ones who break out of the trade-time-for-money trap all run the same simple math test.

The rule:

Take your monthly revenue target. Divide by 100 hours = the rate you charge now per hour you work.
Divide that same target by 25 hours = your LIFE-BACK RATE, the rate that lets you coach for the life you actually want.

$15K target. 100 hours = $150/hr. 25 hours = $600/hr. The gap between those two is your price problem.

And yes, you can charge that. The coaches I studied doing $15K at 25 hours a week aren't smarter. They aren't better trainers. They priced for the life they wanted. Not the hours they had.

Run the math tonight. If the gap is more than 20%, raise your prices in the next 30 days. Pick a date now.
